statusDetail: Coverage complete: all 58 catalog checks have conclusive outcomes. Representative coverage includes home, listing, detail, reader, search, login, registration, and recovery; checkout/payment completion, post-auth account management, adult surfaces, community, and every genre template were not covered because they require credentials/commitment or duplicate the sampled catalog templates.

page.framework: server-rendered legacy MPA with jQuery, Axios, Swiper and Slick

paths.description: Homepage and discovery hub, representing global navigation, promotions, search entry, and merchandising.
Free-comics listing, representing a high-traffic catalog/list template.
Book detail page, representing product metadata, purchase/sample actions, and recommendations.
Free sample reader reached from the product, representing completion of the primary try-before-purchase flow.
Detailed search, representing the principal form-heavy discovery workflow.
Login redirect on member.cmoa.jp, representing authentication and account access.
Registration entry page, representing account creation choices.
A deliberately missing route, representing HTTP/navigation recovery.

findings.summary: The public catalog is light-only.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is visually identical to the light surface, and the CSS probe reports color-scheme: normal with a white body.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and retint surfaces, text, controls, imagery, and browser chrome with prefers-color-scheme/light-dark().

findings.summary: Navigation and content changes do not use authored view transitions.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no authored view-transition rules; representative page changes are full abrupt swaps.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressively enhanced same- and cross-document View Transitions for catalog-to-detail and state changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Long pages provide static chrome with no scroll-position feedback.
findings.evidence: The homepage is over 11,000 CSS px tall, while DOM/CSS inspection found no scroll-state container query or progress treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Use sticky, scroll-state-aware navigation or a lightweight progress/return affordance on long catalog pages.

findings.summary: Header menus are manually positioned rather than anchored.
findings.evidence: CSS places sideRightMenu absolutely at top:69px/right:14px and the account menu at fixed offsets; no anchor-name/position-anchor/position-try was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS anchor positioning with position-try fallbacks for menus and popovers.

findings.summary: Custom div menus replace semantic dismissible primitives.
findings.evidence: The probe found zero dialog, popover, or details elements while DOM CSS shows class-toggled custom menu overlays and close controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Move transient menus to popover and modal flows to dialog, preserving focus and declarative light-dismiss.

findings.summary: Dense promotional chrome crowds the actual catalog.
findings.evidence: The first mobile-scaled viewport contains multiple navigation bars, a safety-search block, sidebar calls to action, and several stacked campaign banners before/alongside core books.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce simultaneous promotions, simplify repeated navigation, and reserve first-view emphasis for search, free reading, and the leading catalog content.

findings.summary: Mobile receives a 1024px desktop layout scaled down to fit.
findings.evidence: At a 360x800 emulation, layout metrics report clientWidth/innerWidth 1024 because the viewport is width=1024; screenshots show tiny desktop text and controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Use width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and rebuild the 990px fixed shell with fluid grids, intrinsic sizing, and responsive navigation.

findings.summary: Reusable catalog components do not adapt at component level.
findings.evidence: The probe found zero container rules; authored CSS repeatedly fixes the main shell and common regions at 990px.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards, sidebars, and navigation containment and adapt them with size container queries.

findings.summary: Many controls are too small for touch.
findings.evidence: The probe counted 120 visible targets below 24px in one dimension, Lighthouse failed target-size, and the scaled mobile shell makes controls materially smaller.
findings.suggestedFix: Meet WCAG target sizing/spacing, preserve visible focus, and provide non-hover states after correcting the viewport.

findings.summary: Lab Core Web Vitals are poor.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 16.3s, CLS 0.662, TBT 230ms and performance 0.33; an unconstrained desktop trace was faster (LCP 1.41s), showing the mobile/throttled risk.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize and preload the real LCP asset, remove redirect/critical-chain delay, reserve dynamic space, and set performance budgets.

findings.summary: Late content causes major layout shift under mobile lab conditions.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported CLS 0.662 and two layout shifts; the image audit found 31 homepage images without dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width/height or aspect-ratio to every image/banner slot and stabilize fonts and late promotions.

findings.summary: JavaScript startup is heavy.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported 2.6s main-thread work and 1.3s JavaScript execution; the page loads 58 scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove redundant tags/libraries, defer non-critical code, and split remaining work into prioritized tasks.

findings.summary: The critical path and caching are inefficient.
findings.evidence: HAR confirms parser-inserted blocking jQuery, Axios and cookie scripts plus five stylesheets; Lighthouse estimates 1.03s render-blocking and 2,209KiB cache savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-critical scripts, inline only critical CSS, compress text, use durable immutable caching, and optimize LCP discovery.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused and duplicate client code.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 862KiB unused JavaScript and 13KiB unused CSS; DOM inspection shows duplicate Axios, jquery.cookie, Yahoo and LINE/TikTok loaders.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate tag loading, remove duplicate libraries, and conditionally load recommendation/marketing code after intent or consent.

findings.summary: Forms, links, and images have incomplete accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails image-alt, input-image-alt and link-name; search inspection found unlabeled text/select fields, and the detail image audit found 74 images without alt.
findings.suggestedFix: Add programmatic labels and discernible control/link names; give meaningful images concise alt and decorative images alt="".

findings.summary: Text and controls fail minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed color-contrast, while the contrast-preference screenshot remains unchanged from default.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct failing color pairs to WCAG AA and add forced-colors/prefers-contrast adaptations without removing system colors.

findings.summary: Document structure is incomplete for assistive navigation.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports non-sequential headings and no main landmark; the page jumps from H2/H3 to H4 and uses many role-bearing fragments without a main region.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one main landmark, make heading levels reflect the visual hierarchy, and test the full keyboard focus order.

findings.summary: The scaled desktop layout makes text illegible on phones.
findings.evidence: The 360px screenshots render a 1024px canvas at 0.3516 scale, reducing already-small 9px to 13px labels to a few physical pixels.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct the viewport and establish fluid type/spacing with readable minimum sizes and line heights.

findings.summary: Viewport policy and fixed layout obstruct zoom and reflow.
findings.evidence: Homepage uses width=1024; the login viewport includes maximum-scale=1 and user-scalable=0; Lighthouse fails meta-viewport and target-size.
findings.suggestedFix: Use device-width with unrestricted zoom and ensure content reflows at 320 CSS px and 200% zoom.

findings.summary: The homepage logs browser errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse explicitly failed errors-in-console; HAR also records blocked/aborted marketing requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove uncaught errors, gate optional integrations, and handle blocked third-party requests without console noise.

findings.summary: Image dimensions and asset structure are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 31 homepage and 42 detail images missing dimensions; Lighthouse also failed unsized-images.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit dimensions/aspect ratios from the content system and validate generated markup in CI.

findings.summary: Chrome reports platform hygiene problems.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed inspector-issues and BFCache with three failure reasons; the page also loads many legacy scripts and duplicated integrations.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve DevTools issues and BFCache blockers, update dependencies, and avoid unload/state patterns that prevent restoration.

findings.summary: Some links are not crawlable despite strong server rendering.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed crawlable-anchors. This coexists with 100% raw-content coverage and hundreds of valid href links, so the defect is limited rather than a JS-shell failure.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace JavaScript-only or malformed link destinations with real href URLs and descriptive text.

findings.summary: Transport policy and cookie attributes are weak.
findings.evidence: HTTPS and frame-ancestors are present, but HSTS and nosniff are missing; 27 of 29 cookies lack Secure and many use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Enable HSTS and nosniff, harden CSP beyond frame-ancestors, and mark every HTTPS cookie Secure with the narrowest SameSite/HttpOnly policy.

findings.summary: Tracking and third-party collection are excessive on first load.
findings.evidence: The tracker capture sees 42 third-party origins and Google, Facebook, DoubleClick, TikTok, Twitter, LINE, Yahoo and others; HAR records 328 third-party requests and about 5.09MB transferred.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize vendors, load analytics only after lawful consent/intent, batch essential telemetry, and proxy or self-host where justified.

findings.summary: Authentication offers password and federated identity but no phishing-resistant passkey path.
findings.evidence: The login screenshot exposes email/password and six social identity choices; inspected auth markup contains no WebAuthn/passkey signal. No permission prompt fired on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Add passkey registration, conditional authentication, recovery, and reauthentication alongside existing methods.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers lack HSTS, Referrer-Policy and nosniff; Permissions-Policy only grants client-hint features and CSP only sets frame-ancestors.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive script/style CSP with nonces or hashes, HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, a deny-by-default Permissions-Policy, and Trusted Types where feasible.

findings.summary: Custom fixed-offset overlays are fragile at viewport edges.
findings.evidence: Header dropdowns are class-toggled absolute boxes with fixed widths/offsets and no anchor fallback; the main site is fixed at 990px.
findings.suggestedFix: Use top-layer popovers/dialogs and anchor positioning with fallbacks, and preserve state/focus during DOM changes.

findings.summary: Search and sign-in input assistance is incomplete.
findings.evidence: Search fields have empty autocomplete and no programmatic labels; homepage search explicitly disables autocomplete.
findings.suggestedFix: Use correct labels and autocomplete tokens, including username/current-password or WebAuthn on sign-in and suitable search semantics.

findings.summary: Image delivery is wasteful.
findings.evidence: Of 100 homepage images, 99 use legacy formats, 35 are oversized, 53 lack srcset and 70 below-fold images are not lazy; images transfer 3.31MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants, responsive srcset/sizes, dimensions and native lazy loading, retaining quality-appropriate fallbacks.

findings.summary: Background marketing work dominates a page view.
findings.evidence: The load makes 330 requests and runs repeated vendor loaders, with Lighthouse estimating 862KiB unused JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate vendor tags, defer non-essential work until idle/intent/consent, and stop background collection when hidden.

findings.summary: Third-party script cost is disproportionate to visible user value.
findings.evidence: Tag Manager/gtag transfer more than 500KB, TikTok variants over 300KB, Facebook 175KB, amid 42 third-party origins; total load is 5.13MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, consolidate analytics, and lazy-load optional media and integrations.

taskList.title: Replace the fixed 1024px/990px desktop shell with a genuinely responsive, zoomable layout
Cut startup cost and stabilize the LCP/CLS path
Reduce and consent-gate the analytics and advertising footprint
Repair accessible labels, names, landmarks, headings, contrast, and target sizing
Modernize responsive image delivery and reserve image space
Simplify promotional chrome and use semantic top-layer controls
Add user preference and modern interaction support
Add passkeys and correct autofill/input assistance
Resolve console, DevTools, BFCache, and crawlable-link defects
